claim: Human organogenesis is when severe developmental abnormalities commonly originate.
source: Human organogenesis is when severe developmental abnormalities commonly originate.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about developmental biology.

claim: Understanding human organogenesis has relied upon inference from patient phenotypes and assumptions from in vitro stem cell models and non-human vertebrates.
source: However, understanding this critical embryonic phase has relied upon inference from patient phenotypes and assumptions from in vitro stem cell models and non-human vertebrates.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field based on established knowledge.

claim: The study reports an integrated transcriptomic atlas of human organogenesis.
source: We report an integrated transcriptomic atlas of human organogenesis.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the manuscript, supported by the data presented throughout.

claim: Lineage-guided principal components analysis uncovered novel relatedness of particular developmental genes across different organs and tissues.
source: By lineage-guided principal components analysis, we uncover novel relatedness of particular developmental genes across different organs and tissues
evidence: This claim is supported by the LgPCA analysis presented in Figure 2 and related text.

claim: The study identified unique transcriptional codes which correctly predicted the cause of many congenital disorders.
source: By lineage-guided principal components analysis, we uncover novel relatedness of particular developmental genes across different organs and tissues and identified unique transcriptional codes which correctly predicted the cause of many congenital disorders.
evidence: This is supported by the analysis in Figure 3 and Supplementary file 1H showing prediction of causative genes.

claim: The model pinpoints co-enriched genes as new causes of developmental disorders such as cleft palate and congenital heart disease.
source: By inference, our model pinpoints co-enriched genes as new causes of developmental disorders such as cleft palate and congenital heart disease.
evidence: This is based on inference from the LgPCA analysis and is speculative regarding novel causative genes.

claim: The data revealed more than 6000 novel transcripts.
source: The data revealed more than 6000 novel transcripts
evidence: This is directly supported by the transcript assembly data presented in Figure 4 and Supplementary file 1I.

claim: Over 90% of the novel transcripts fulfil criteria as long non-coding RNAs.
source: The data revealed more than 6000 novel transcripts, over 90% of which fulfil criteria as long non-coding RNAs
evidence: This is supported by the CPAT analysis shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The novel long non-coding RNAs are correlated with the protein-coding genome over megabase distances.
source: over 90% of which fulfil criteria as long non-coding RNAs correlated with the protein-coding genome over megabase distances.
evidence: This is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 4e-h.

claim: Previous transcriptomics post-implantation have sampled either the whole embryo by expression microarray, lacking organ-specific resolution and the vast majority of long non-coding transcription.
source: Previous transcriptomics post-implantation have sampled either the whole embryo by expression microarray (Fang et al., 2010), thus lacking organ-specific resolution and the vast majority of long non-coding (lnc) transcription
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Previous studies included lnc expression by RNA-seq but focused on single sites such as limb bud or pancreas.
source: or included lnc expression by massively parallel short-read RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) but focussed on single sites such as limb bud (Cotney et al., 2013) or pancreas (Cebola et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: RNA-seq from NIH Roadmap and other studies during or after the end of the first trimester falls after the embryonic period.
source: RNA-seq from NIH Roadmap and other studies during or after the end of the first trimester of pregnancy falls after the embryonic period (which ends at 56–58 days post-conception (Carnegie Stage 23))
evidence: This is based on citation to NIH Roadmap studies and established knowledge about embryonic development timing.

claim: The embryonic period ends at 56-58 days post-conception (Carnegie Stage 23).
source: (which ends at 56–58 days post-conception (Carnegie Stage 23))
evidence: This is established knowledge about human embryonic development.

claim: NIH Roadmap fetal data commonly reflects near terminal differentiation within heterogeneous fetal organs and tissues.
source: RNA-seq from NIH Roadmap and other studies during or after the end of the first trimester of pregnancy falls after the embryonic period (which ends at 56–58 days post-conception (Carnegie Stage 23)) and commonly reflects near terminal differentiation within heterogeneous fetal organs and tissues (Jaffe et al., 2015; Roadmap Epigenomics Consortium, 2015; Roost et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Fifteen human embryonic sites were sampled for transcriptomic analysis.
source: Organs and tissues from fifteen human embryonic sites were sequenced in two sets of biological replicates (except pancreas and tongue) to generate 28 strand-specific RNA-seq datasets
evidence: This is directly supported by the experimental design described and shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The study generated 28 strand-specific RNA-seq datasets.
source: Organs and tissues from fifteen human embryonic sites were sequenced in two sets of biological replicates (except pancreas and tongue) to generate 28 strand-specific RNA-seq datasets
evidence: This is directly stated in the methods and supported by Supplementary file 1A.

claim: Each replicate had 44-90 million uniquely mapped reads.
source: Organs and tissues from fifteen human embryonic sites were sequenced in two sets of biological replicates (except pancreas and tongue) to generate 28 strand-specific RNA-seq datasets with 44–90 million uniquely mapped reads per replicate
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Supplementary file 1A.

claim: Approximately 70% of protein-coding genes contained 100-10,000 mapped reads.
source: Global transcription rates across all organs and tissues were comparable over a high dynamic range; approximately 70% of protein-coding genes contained 100–10,000 mapped reads (Figure 1b; Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: There were three-fold the number of differentially expressed genes in the fetal datasets compared to embryonic datasets.
source: There were three-fold the number of differentially expressed genes in the fetal datasets but equivalent enrichment of gene ontology (GO) terms in the embryo
evidence: This is supported by the comparison analysis shown in Figure 1c and Supplementary file 1B-C.

claim: Embryonic datasets showed equivalent enrichment of gene ontology terms compared to fetal datasets.
source: There were three-fold the number of differentially expressed genes in the fetal datasets but equivalent enrichment of gene ontology (GO) terms in the embryo
evidence: This is supported by the GO analysis shown in Figure 1c and Supplementary file 1C.

claim: Embryonic datasets showed enrichment for early developmental processes such as morphogenesis of an epithelial bud, anterior/posterior pattern specification and embryonic morphogenesis.
source: including many early developmental processes such as morphogenesis of an epithelial bud, anterior/posterior pattern specification and embryonic morphogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by the GO analysis shown in Figure 1c and Supplementary file 1C.

claim: Fetal datasets showed enrichment for homeostatic processes.
source: These were in contrast to homeostatic processes enriched in the fetal dataset (Figure 1c; Supplementary file 1B–C).
evidence: This is supported by the GO analysis shown in Figure 1c and Supplementary file 1C.

claim: ZNF and ZSCAN family members were broadly expressed across human embryonic tissues.
source: While ZNF and ZSCAN family members were broadly expressed discrete site-specific expression was more apparent for individual members of other transcription factor families (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is supported by the heatmap shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Individual members of other transcription factor families showed discrete site-specific expression.
source: While ZNF and ZSCAN family members were broadly expressed discrete site-specific expression was more apparent for individual members of other transcription factor families (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) exemplified by the HOX gene clusters (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 1d.

claim: HOX gene clusters exemplify discrete site-specific expression.
source: discrete site-specific expression was more apparent for individual members of other transcription factor families (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) exemplified by the HOX gene clusters (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: User-defined sets of up to five developmental transcription factors characteristic for a particular organ or tissue displayed very high levels of tissue specificity.
source: User-defined sets of up to five developmental transcription factors characteristic for a particular organ or tissue displayed very high levels of tissue specificity (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by the validation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Principal components analysis grouped biological replicates but did not resolve relationships between different organs and tissues other than the distinctiveness of brain and liver.
source: However, while principal components (PC) analysis (PCA) or clustering grouped biological replicates, relationships between different organs and tissues other than the distinctiveness of brain and liver were not resolved (Figure 1—figure supplements 3–4).
evidence: This is supported by the PCA and clustering analyses shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 3-4.

claim: Non-negative matrix factorisation identified eleven non-overlapping 'metagenes' from the complete expression dataset.
source: By setting the parameters such that representative genes were only extracted once, we identified eleven non-overlapping 'metagenes' from the complete expression dataset with clear tissue-specific signals for thyroid, liver, RPE, brain, heart and adrenal gland (Figure 1—figure supplement 5; Supplementary file 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the NMF analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: NMF metagenes showed clear tissue-specific signals for thyroid, liver, RPE, brain, heart and adrenal gland.
source: we identified eleven non-overlapping 'metagenes' from the complete expression dataset with clear tissue-specific signals for thyroid, liver, RPE, brain, heart and adrenal gland (Figure 1—figure supplement 5; Supplementary file 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the NMF analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: Metagene 2 consists of 39 genes indicative of human embryonic liver.
source: From this starting point, we wanted to move beyond the unique organ-specific signatures to study how patterns of gene expression co-varied across tissues. While relaxing NMF parameters would allow non-exclusive gene selection across metagenes, we also wanted to capture differences in gene expression between organs (e.g. aspects of what is not expressed as a contributing factor to an organ's identity). Moreover, different embryonic organs are related according to developmental lineage. We reasoned that being able to apply a lineage structure would create natural assemblies of co-regulated genes (Figure 2a). Accordingly, we adapted a method from spatial ecology and phylogenetics (Jombart et al., 2010a, 2010b) to constrain PCA by imposing a hierarchical developmental lineage and termed this approach LgPCA.
evidence: This is inferred from the NMF analysis and the description of metagene 2 in the context of Figure 1—figure supplement 5b.

claim: Stem cell-derived hepatocytes and primary hepatocytes showed clear enrichment for metagene 2 genes.
source: Clear enrichment for the stem cell-derived hepatocytes and the primary hepatocytes (but not the fibroblasts) was apparent in metagene 2, the cluster of 39 genes indicative of human embryonic liver.
evidence: This is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5b.

claim: Human embryonic fibroblasts did not show enrichment for metagene 2 genes.
source: Clear enrichment for the stem cell-derived hepatocytes and the primary hepatocytes (but not the fibroblasts) was apparent in metagene 2
evidence: This is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5b.

claim: The study adapted a method from spatial ecology and phylogenetics to constrain PCA by imposing a hierarchical developmental lineage.
source: Accordingly, we adapted a method from spatial ecology and phylogenetics (Jombart et al., 2010a, 2010b) to constrain PCA by imposing a hierarchical developmental lineage and termed this approach LgPCA.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the original methods and description of the adaptation.

claim: The adapted method was termed LgPCA (Lineage-guided Principal Components Analysis).
source: we adapted a method from spatial ecology and phylogenetics (Jombart et al., 2010a, 2010b) to constrain PCA by imposing a hierarchical developmental lineage and termed this approach LgPCA.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the text.

claim: The study included RNA-seq from undifferentiated human embryonic stem cells to represent pre-gastrulation human biology.
source: We also included RNA-seq from undifferentiated human embryonic stem cells (Roadmap Epigenomics Consortium, 2015) to represent pre-gastrulation human biology.
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by citation.

claim: LgPCA generated thirty-one principal components.
source: Of the total thirty-one principal components (PCs) arising from LgPCA
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The first fifteen principal components from LgPCA identified patterns of gene expression across groups of related tissues and unique organ-specific signatures.
source: Of the total thirty-one principal components (PCs) arising from LgPCA the first fifteen now identified patterns of gene expression across groups of related tissues in addition to unique organ-specific signatures (Figure 2b)
evidence: This is supported by the LgPCA analysis shown in Figure 2b.

claim: PCs 16-31 from LgPCA sampled heterogeneity within individual organs and tissues.
source: while PCs 16–31 sampled heterogeneity within individual organs and tissues (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: PC1 high loadings represent pluripotency.
source: In keeping with this transition PCs 1–4 ordered samples reminiscent of very early developmental events: pluripotency (extreme positive loadings in PC1; 'PC1 high')
evidence: This is supported by the LgPCA analysis and the inclusion of ESC data.

claim: PC2 low loadings represent early brain formation.
source: early brain formation (extreme negative loadings in PC2; 'PC2 low')
evidence: This is inferred from the LgPCA analysis shown in Figure 2b.

claim: PC4 low loadings represent foregut endoderm.
source: foregut endoderm (PC4 low)
evidence: This is inferred from the LgPCA analysis shown in Figure 2b.

claim: PC4 high loadings represent intermediate mesoderm.
source: and intermediate mesoderm (PC4 high).
evidence: This is inferred from the LgPCA analysis shown in Figure 2b.

claim: PCs 5-15 resolved individual organs and tissues.
source: PCs 5–15 resolved the individual organs and tissues
evidence: This is supported by the LgPCA analysis shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Low PC5 loadings discriminated liver from other foregut endoderm derivatives.
source: for instance low PC5 loadings discriminated liver from the other foregut endoderm derivatives.
evidence: This is supported by the LgPCA analysis shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The 1000 genes with the most extreme loadings in PCs 1-15 were interrogated for regulatory networks based on enrichment of transcription factor motifs.
source: We undertook this in two different ways, both based on studying the 1000 genes with the most extreme loadings in PCs 1–15 that identified gene co-expression patterns across tissues and within individual organs (Figure 2b; Supplementary file 1E). We interrogated these gene sets for regulatory networks based on the enrichment of transcription factor motifs (Janky et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by the iRegulon analysis described and shown in Figure 3a.

claim: iRegulon analysis recovered numerous well known master regulators alongside previously unappreciated factors.
source: Numerous well known master regulators were recovered alongside previously unappreciated factors for either broad tissue groups (e.g. foregut endoderm derivatives) or individual organs (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is supported by the iRegulon analysis shown in Figure 3a.

claim: NANOG, OCT4 and MYC are proven regulators of human pluripotency.
source: As proof-of-principle, this also included proven regulators of human pluripotency, NANOG, OCT4 and MYC, at an extreme of PC1.
evidence: This is established knowledge about pluripotency regulators.

claim: NANOG, OCT4 and MYC were identified at an extreme of PC1.
source: As proof-of-principle, this also included proven regulators of human pluripotency, NANOG, OCT4 and MYC, at an extreme of PC1.
evidence: This is supported by the iRegulon analysis shown in Figure 3a.

claim: In several instances approaching half of the 1000 genes with the most extreme PC loadings imputed co-regulation by a single transcription factor.
source: Remarkably, in several instances approaching half of the 1000 genes with the most extreme PC loadings imputed co-regulation by a single transcription factor, such as HNF4A in the liver or SRF in the heart.
evidence: This is supported by the iRegulon analysis shown in Figure 3a.

claim: HNF4A co-regulates approximately half of the most extreme genes in liver.
source: such as HNF4A in the liver
evidence: This is supported by the iRegulon analysis shown in Figure 3a.

claim: SRF co-regulates approximately half of the most extreme genes in heart.
source: or SRF in the heart.
evidence: This is supported by the iRegulon analysis shown in Figure 3a.

claim: The data predicted RUNX and BAD as novel regulators of human adrenal and gonadal development.
source: Alongside NR5A1, the data predicted RUNX and BAD as novel regulators of human adrenal and gonadal development (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is a prediction based on the iRegulon analysis shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Transcription factors comprised typically less than 5% of the 1000 most extreme genes in PCs 1-15.
source: As a second approach to study gene regulation, we extracted the transcription factors (typically <5%) from amongst the 1000 most extreme genes in PCs 1–15 (Supplementary file 1G).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Supplementary file 1G.

claim: In 309 out of 594 instances there was a relevant mouse mutation phenotype supporting the transcription factors identified by LgPCA as key regulators of human organogenesis.
source: We searched the Mouse Genome Informatics database (MGI) and in 309/594 instances there was a relevant mouse mutation phenotype supporting the notion that the transcription factors identified by LgPCA are key regulators of human organogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by comparison with the MGI database as described.

claim: At the lowest extreme of PC5 (liver) the twenty-two transcription factors contained all three of those required for reprogramming fibroblasts directly to hepatocytes.
source: At the lowest extreme of PC5 (liver) the twenty-two transcription factors contained all three of those required for reprogramming fibroblasts directly to hepatocytes (Huang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published reprogramming factors.

claim: The extreme PC loadings in the LgPCA data prioritized transcription factors responsible for major congenital disorders.
source: In keeping with these regulatory roles, the extreme PC loadings in the LgPCA data also prioritized those transcription factors responsible for major congenital disorders (Supplementary file 1G).
evidence: This is supported by the analysis shown in Supplementary file 1G.

claim: LgPCA can predict multisystem abnormalities such as the combined heart and limb defects of Holt-Oram syndrome.
source: Because LgPCA is not limited to individual organs this included a novel ability to predict multisystem abnormalities such as the combined heart and limb defects of Holt-Oram syndrome (OMIM 142900, TBX5, PC13 low)
evidence: This is supported by the LgPCA analysis identifying TBX5 at PC13 low.

claim: Holt-Oram syndrome (OMIM 142900) is caused by mutations in TBX5.
source: such as the combined heart and limb defects of Holt-Oram syndrome (OMIM 142900, TBX5, PC13 low)
evidence: This is established knowledge about the genetic cause of Holt-Oram syndrome.

claim: TBX5 is found at PC13 low in the LgPCA analysis.
source: (OMIM 142900, TBX5, PC13 low)
evidence: This is supported by the LgPCA analysis.

claim: Palate and limb abnormalities are associated with mutations in TP63 (OMIM 603543).
source: or the palate and limb abnormalities associated with mutations in TP63 (OMIM 603543, PC3 high).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the genetic cause of this syndrome.

claim: TP63 is found at PC3 high in the LgPCA analysis.
source: or the palate and limb abnormalities associated with mutations in TP63 (OMIM 603543, PC3 high).
evidence: This is supported by the LgPCA analysis.

claim: Mutations in genes encoding transcription factors are over-represented causes of congenital disorders.
source: Mutations in genes encoding transcription factors are over-represented causes of congenital disorders, most likely due to their critical function during organogenesis and inadequacy when haploinsufficient.
evidence: This is established knowledge in developmental genetics.

claim: Transcription factors are critical during organogenesis and inadequate when haploinsufficient.
source: most likely due to their critical function during organogenesis and inadequacy when haploinsufficient.
evidence: This is established knowledge about transcription factor function.

claim: 53 disorders were suitable for assessment with an average critical region of 13.7 Mb each containing an average of 111 protein-coding genes.
source: 53 disorders were suitable for assessment with an average critical region of 13.7 Mb each containing an average of 111 protein-coding genes (Supplementary file 1H).

claim: In 37 instances (73%) LgPCA uniquely selected the correct transcription factor.
source: Strikingly, in 37 instances (73%) LgPCA uniquely selected the correct transcription factor
evidence: This is supported by the validation analysis shown in Supplementary file 1H.

claim: In 48 instances (91%) LgPCA narrowed the field down to three or fewer transcription factors.
source: and in 48 instances (91%) narrowed the field down to three or fewer transcription factors.
evidence: This is supported by the validation analysis shown in Supplementary file 1H.

claim: LgPCA predicts DLX5, DLX6, LHX8 and FOXF2 as causative genes in cleft palate.
source: When applied to 13 syndromes (mostly deletion disorders) where the causative gene remains unresolved clear predictions of causality emerge, for instance in cleft palate (DLX5, DLX6, LHX8 and FOXF2)

claim: LgPCA predicts ZIC1 and ZIC4 as causative genes in cerebellar disorders.
source: or cerebellar disorders (ZIC1 and ZIC4) (Supplementary file 1H).
evidence: This is a prediction based on the LgPCA analysis shown in Supplementary file 1H.

source: Frequently, there is an appropriate mutant mouse phenotype such as CASZ1 in cardiac malformations, part of Chr1p36 deletion syndrome

claim: SOX10 is predicted to be involved in 46,XX disorder of sex differentiation linked to duplication on Chr22.
source: or SOX10 in the 46,XX disorder of sex differentiation (DSD) linked to duplication on Chr22 (Figure 3b and Supplementary file 1H).
evidence: This is a prediction based on the LgPCA analysis and mouse phenotype data shown in Figure 3b and Supplementary file 1H.

claim: 81 out of 1571 genes enriched in embryogenesis compared to fetal datasets were annotated long intergenic non-coding transcripts.
source: A dedicated programme operating during human organogenesis seemed likely as 81 out of the 1571 genes enriched in embryogenesis compared to the fetal datasets were annotated long intergenic non-coding (LINC) transcripts (Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the differential expression analysis shown in Supplementary file 1B.

claim: The study assembled strand-specific transcripts not recognized by GENCODE 18 annotation.
source: To look beyond this we assembled strand-specific transcripts not recognized by current genome annotation [GENCODE 18 (Harrow et al., 2012)]
evidence: This is supported by the transcript assembly methods described.

claim: Novel transcripts were systematically named according to recommended criteria.
source: and systematically named them individually according to recommended criteria (Mattick and Rinn, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to naming guidelines.

claim: 6251 unique loci accounted for in excess of 9 Mb of novel polyadenylated transcription from the human genome.
source: 6251 unique loci accounted for in excess of 9 Mb of novel polyadenylated transcription from the human genome (Figure 4a and Supplementary file 1I).

claim: LncRNA criteria include an absence of reads spanning splice junctions to currently annotated genes.
source: and an absence of reads spanning splice junctions to currently annotated genes (Mattick and Rinn, 2015).

claim: Novel lncRNAs were classified as bidirectional, antisense, overlapping, or intergenic according to orientation and position relative to the annotated genome.
source: These lncRNAs were classified as either bidirectional, antisense or overlapping, or by exclusion intergenic, according to orientation and position in relation to the annotated genome (Mattick and Rinn, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to classification guidelines.

claim: Novel transcripts were most commonly 500-1,500 bp but could extend to over 600 Kb.
source: Transcripts were most commonly 500–1,500 bp but could extend to over 600 Kb (Figure 4c)
evidence: This is supported by the size distribution shown in Figure 4c.

source: and showed high tissue-specificity with the median Tau value (Yanai et al., 2005) of 0.86

source: much higher than for protein-coding genes (0.63)

claim: Previously annotated non-coding genes have a median Tau value of 0.89.
source: but consistent with previously annotated non-coding genes (0.89).
evidence: This is supported by the Tau analysis.

claim: Reduced physical distance to expressed annotated genes markedly increased the likelihood of novel transcript co-expression.
source: We investigated the association between this novel human embryonic transcriptome and the annotated genome. Reduced physical distance to expressed annotated genes markedly increased the likelihood of novel transcript co-expression (Figure 4e)
evidence: This is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 4e.

claim: The best correlations between novel transcripts and annotated genes were not always with the closest gene.
source: although the best correlations were by no means always with the closest gene (Figure 4f–g).
evidence: This is supported by the examples shown in Figure 4f-g.

claim: The median distance to the closest annotated gene was 7.7 Kb.
source: The median distance to the closest annotated gene was 7.7 Kb (Figure 4—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is supported by the distance analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: On average the best correlation was at 188 Kb.
source: while on average the best correlation was at 188 Kb (random prediction was 476 Kb).
evidence: This is supported by the correlation analysis.

claim: Random prediction for best correlation distance was 476 Kb.
source: (random prediction was 476 Kb).

claim: Over half (3634) of the lnc transcripts were classified positionally as LINC RNAs.
source: Over half (3634) of the lnc transcripts were classified positionally as LINC RNAs.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by the classification shown in Figure 4a.

claim: HE-LINC-C7T121 shows correlation with TBX20 over a 2 Mb window on chromosome 7.
source: As a first step, the multi-tissue nature of our dataset allowed intricate correlative patterns to be deciphered implying putative relationships; for instance over a 2 Mb window and across numerous genes on chromosome 7 between HE-LINC-C7T121 and TBX20, which encodes a developmental cardiac transcription factor mutated in a wide range of congenital heart disease (Figure 4h).
evidence: This is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 4h.

claim: TBX20 encodes a developmental cardiac transcription factor mutated in a wide range of congenital heart disease.
source: TBX20, which encodes a developmental cardiac transcription factor mutated in a wide range of congenital heart disease
evidence: This is established knowledge about TBX20.

claim: This is the first comprehensive transcriptomic atlas during human organogenesis.
source: Taken together, this study reports the first comprehensive transcriptomic atlas during human organogenesis to complement parallel initiatives from later development and adulthood (Jaffe et al., 2015; Roadmap Epigenomics Consortium, 2015; Roost et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study supported by comparison with other initiatives.

claim: The method of analysis incorporated developmental lineage to decipher novel genetic signatures.
source: Subjecting transcription from many sites to a method of analysis that incorporated developmental lineage deciphered novel genetic signatures
evidence: This is supported by the LgPCA methodology and results.

claim: The analysis predicted causality in many human developmental disorders.
source: predicted causality in many human developmental disorders
evidence: This is supported by the validation analysis shown in Figure 3b and Supplementary file 1H.

claim: The analysis associated novel non-coding transcription with expression from the surrounding protein-coding genome.
source: and associated novel non-coding transcription with expression from the surrounding protein-coding genome.
evidence: This is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 4e-h.

claim: The data arise from a relatively narrow window of embryonic development.
source: At present, the data arise from a relatively narrow window of embryonic development but set the stage for future longitudinal studies for individual organs over time.
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged by the authors.

claim: The tiny amounts and scarcity of human embryonic tissue necessitated aspects of pooling across different Carnegie stages for some sites.
source: The tiny amounts and scarcity of human embryonic tissue also necessitated aspects of pooling across different Carnegie stages for some sites
evidence: This is a methodological limitation described by the authors.

claim: Pooling across Carnegie stages had no impact on ascertaining organ and tissue-specific transcriptomic signatures by LgPCA.
source: but it is striking that this had no impact on ascertaining organ and tissue-specific transcriptomic signatures by LgPCA.
evidence: This is an inference from the successful LgPCA results despite pooling.

claim: The integrated data are expected to be valuable to stem cell researchers examining the fidelity of PSC differentiation in vitro.
source: The integrated data are expected to be particularly valuable to stem cell researchers examining the fidelity of PSC differentiation in vitro
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications.

claim: The integrated data are expected to be valuable for searching for transcription factors for direct reprogramming of chosen cell lineages.
source: or searching for transcription factors for direct reprogramming of chosen cell lineages.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications supported by the hepatocyte reprogramming example.

claim: The discovery of a major new programme of non-coding transcription adds a fresh layer of detail on the spatiotemporal regulation of the human genome.
source: Finally, the discovery of a major new programme of non-coding transcription adds a fresh layer of detail on the spatiotemporal regulation of the human genome.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by the novel transcript data in Figure 4.

claim: Human embryonic material was collected under ethical approval, informed consent and according to the Codes of Practice of the Human Tissue Authority.
source: Human embryonic material was collected under ethical approval, informed consent and according to the Codes of Practice of the Human Tissue Authority and staged by the Carnegie classification as described previously (Jennings et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about ethical compliance.

claim: Embryos were staged by the Carnegie classification.
source: and staged by the Carnegie classification as described previously (Jennings et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by citation.

claim: RNA sequencing libraries were generated using the TruSeq Stranded mRNA assay.
source: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) libraries were generated using the TruSeq Stranded mRNA assay (Illumina, Inc.) according to the manufacturer's protocol.
evidence: This is a methodological statement.

claim: The RNA-seq was conducted in three batches at different times.
source: The RNA-seq was conducted in three batches at different times as a necessity of how human embryonic tissue was collected over time (Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by Supplementary file 1A.

claim: Where organs were sequenced across batches, biological replicates clustered together.
source: Where organs were sequenced across batches (palate, RPE, kidney, testis, adrenal gland, heart / left ventricle and liver) biological replicates clustered together (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by the clustering analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: RNA-seq reads were mapped to the human genome (hg19) strand-specifically using TopHat 2.0.9.
source: RNA-seq reads from the Illumina platform were mapped to the human genome (hg19) strand-specifically using TopHat 2.0.9 (Trapnell et al., 2012) and the GENCODE 18 gene annotation set (Harrow et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a methodological statement.

claim: Quantile normalization was used because highly distinct tissues differed strongly on the scale of thousands of genes.
source: Commonly applied RNA-seq normalisation methods such as TMM assume a small proportion of differentially expressed genes in any one dataset (Dillies et al., 2013). Because the highly distinct tissues surveyed here differed strongly on the scale of thousands of genes (for instance liver versus brain) we used quantile normalisation which gave a lower median coefficient of variation than either no or TMM normalization.
evidence: This is a methodological justification supported by citation and comparison.

claim: Quantile normalization gave a lower median coefficient of variation than either no normalization or TMM normalization.
source: we used quantile normalisation which gave a lower median coefficient of variation than either no or TMM normalization.
evidence: This is a methodological justification based on comparison.

claim: NMF was performed using the nmf R package to extract tissue-specific metagenes.
source: NMF was performed using the nmf R package (version NMF_0.20.5) (Gaujoux and Seoighe, 2010) to extract tissue-specific metagenes.
evidence: This is a methodological statement.

claim: The LgPCA approach was adapted from established phylogenetic PCA methodology.
source: The LgPCA approach was adapted from established phylogenetic PCA methodology (Jombart et al., 2010b)
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by citation.

claim: LgPCA was performed using the ppca function from the adephylo R package.
source: and performed using quantile-normalized, gene-level read counts, a high memory (512 Gb) compute node and the ppca function from the adephylo R package (Jombart et al., 2010a).
evidence: This is a methodological statement.

claim: The adephylo R package weighted the principal components by the lineage auto-correlation between samples.
source: A broad user-defined guide tree (Figure 2b) based on well-established knowledge of mammalian gastrulation and downstream lineage relationships was imposed on the different organ and tissue types following which the adephylo R package weighted the principal components by the lineage auto-correlation between samples
evidence: This is a methodological explanation.

claim: The Abouheif distance was used in LgPCA, which takes into account the topology of the specified tree but does not use branch lengths.
source: We used the Abouheif distance as implemented in adephylo (Jombart et al., 2010a), which takes into account the topology of the specified tree but does not use branch lengths.
evidence: This is a methodological statement.

claim: Gene Ontology term enrichment was performed using Fisher's exact test with the elimination algorithm of the R package topGO.
source: For the comparison of the embryonic versus fetal datasets Gene Ontology term enrichment was performed on upregulated genes (FDR < 0.05) using Fisher's exact test with the elimination algorithm of the R package topGO (Alexa and Rahnenfuhrer, 2010).
evidence: This is a methodological statement.

claim: iRegulon is a computational method which tests for enrichment amongst precomputed motif datasets to decipher transcriptional regulatory networks.
source: iRegulon is a computational method which tests for enrichment amongst precomputed motif datasets to decipher transcriptional regulatory networks in a set of co-expressed genes.
evidence: This is a methodological description.

claim: Sample-specific transcriptomes were assembled with Cufflinks version 2.2.0.
source: Sample-specific transcriptomes were assembled with Cufflinks (version 2.2.0) (Trapnell et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a methodological statement.

claim: Bidirectional transcripts were defined as having their TSS within 1 Kb of the TSS of the associated annotated gene.
source: Names were assigned to these novel transcripts following suggested criteria (Mattick and Rinn, 2015) (Figure 4a) with the sole adaptation that bidirectional (BI) transcripts were defined as having their TSS within 1 Kb of the TSS of the associated annotated gene.
evidence: This is a methodological statement about classification criteria.

claim: No transcripts mapped to the same strand within the introns of any annotated gene.
source: No transcripts mapped to the same strand within the introns of any annotated gene excluding the possibility of unspliced transcripts from annotated genes being erroneously defined as novel transcripts.
evidence: This is a quality control statement about the transcript assembly.

claim: A CPAT threshold of >0.2 was used to define 'Transcripts of Uncertain Coding Potential' (TUCP).
source: All transcript sequences (annotated and unannotated) were scored for protein-coding potential using CPAT (based on human training data included with CPAT) (Wang et al., 2013). A threshold of >0.2 was used to define 'Transcripts of Uncertain Coding Potential' (TUCP).
evidence: This is a methodological statement about classification criteria.

claim: Where there were multiple transcripts from a single locus, the longest transcript was retained in assembling the final dataset.
source: Where there were multiple transcripts from a single locus, the longest transcript was retained in assembling the final dataset of 6251 novel transcripts.
evidence: This is a methodological statement about data processing.

claim: The combined dataset included expression of >90% of annotated protein-coding genes (GENCODE18).
source: The combined dataset (black) included expression of >90% of annotated protein-coding genes (GENCODE18 [Harrow et al., 2012]).
evidence: This is stated in the Figure 1 legend and supported by Figure 1b.

claim: Human embryogenesis possesses a distinctive transcriptome compared to fetal datasets.
source: Human embryogenesis possesses a distinctive transcriptome. Human embryonic read counts were compared with equivalent fetal datasets from NIH Roadmap (Roadmap Epigenomics Consortium, 2015) using edgeR (Robinson et al., 2010) and a false discovery rate (FDR) of 0.05
evidence: This is supported by the comparison shown in Figure 1c.
